content:
Trump and Canada trade war takes new turn as latest executive order renames Lake Ontario to Lake America. Google Maps has updated the name, but what you see depends on your location — only US users see "Lake America." Apple Maps still uses the original name...

Lake Ontario is this year's "Gulf of Mexico repeat." Trump signed an executive order last year renaming the latter to "Gulf of America," and has now signed another order to rename the smallest of the Great Lakes, Lake Ontario, to "Lake America."

Canada and most of the rest of the world's reaction has been amusement and mockery. Ontario Premier Doug Ford put up a new large billboard by the lake reading "Lake Ontario. Now and always."

Google Maps has updated its naming, with labels varying depending on your location:

  • US users: Lake America (Lake America)
  • Canadian users: Lake Ontario
  • Rest of the world: Lake Ontario (Lake America)

The approach mirrors how the company handled the Gulf of Mexico. The Associated Press cited a Google blog post stating the company's policy is to use names designated by the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS).

However, Apple Maps has so far stuck with "Lake Ontario," with US users also seeing the original name. Whether it will back down as it did with the Gulf of Mexico remains to be seen. Apple has generally tried to avoid political controversy and has on multiple occasions chosen to accommodate the Trump administration, but with a new CEO, it's unclear whether its stance will change.
